I am a 42-year-old farmer in Afar with no schooling, and this 0.81-hectare sorghum plot is nearly all the land I have. The rains here are scarce and unreliable, but sorghum survives the heat better than maize, so I will plant the seeds I saved from last year's harvest. I cannot afford chemical fertilizer from the town, and it is hard to find here anyway, but I will spread manure from my goats and cattle to make the soil stronger. My wife and children will work this plot together—we do not have money to hire anyone from outside.
